newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says Belgrade protests not internal matter.
newsitem.headline: France says Belgrade protests not internal matter.

text.p: France criticised Serbia for the third day in a row on Wednesday and a key minister said mass demonstrations taking place in Belgrade were no longer an internal Serbian matter.
"What happens in Belgrade is not only an internal matter," European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier told the National Assembly.
"It is a matter that concerns us all because it has to do with democracy, because it has to do with Europe and because it has to do with peace," he said.
"These public demonstrations are impressive both due to their dignity and their calm...They are a sign of a formidable desire for democracy on the part of the Serbian people."
France earlier condemned Belgrade for shutting down two independent radio stations and warned against using force to curb street demonstrations.
Demonstrations which have drawn up to 100,000 protesters a day began after Serbian authorities annulled opposition victories in municipal polls on November 17.

"We very strongly condemn the closing of the two non-government radio stations," foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a news briefing about the closing down of radio stations B-92 and Radio Index.
"We also warn Yugoslav authorities against any use of force (against street demonstrations). The right to information and the right to demonstrate must be respected," Rummelhardt said.

The French Foreign Ministry, citing "extreme concern" at the situation, said on Tuesday: "Authorities in Belgrade should expect a severe warning from the international community if they choose the path of direct confrontation."
